title: The direct sum of two quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal F_1\oplus\mathcal F_2$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal F_1(W)\oplus\mathcal F_2(W)$ (for $W\subseteq X$ open), with componentwise $\mathcal O_X(W)$-module structure and componentwise restriction maps; it is a sheaf, and together with the inclusions and projections of the two summands it is a direct sum (biproduct [def-weil-additive-category]) of $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_2$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$. Then $\mathcal F_1\oplus\mathcal F_2$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BF (lemma-direct-sum-quasi-coherent, whose proof is omitted); the proof follows Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent: on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ the direct sum of the $\widetilde{M_i}$ is $\widetilde{\bigoplus M_i}$) and Section 01LA (section-quasi-coherent), item (3)

proof.text: *The sectionwise binary sum is a sheaf and a coproduct.* Put $\mathcal B(W)=\mathcal F_1(W)\oplus\mathcal F_2(W)$, with componentwise restrictions and $\mathcal O_X(W)$-action as in the statement. A matching family of pairs over an open cover is exactly a matching family in each $\mathcal F_i$; the unique gluings in the two sheaves give the unique gluing in $\mathcal B$. Thus $\mathcal B$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its inclusions $j_i$ and projections $p_i$ satisfy $p_i j_i=\mathrm{id}$, $p_i j_{3-i}=0$, and $j_1p_1+j_2p_2=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ sectionwise [def-weil-additive-category]. For any two module morphisms $f_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal H$, the map $f_1p_1+f_2p_2:\mathcal B\to\mathcal H$ is the unique map whose composites with the $j_i$ are $f_i$, since any $h$ equals $h(j_1p_1+j_2p_2)$. Hence $\mathcal B$ is both the stated biproduct and the coproduct, a colimit of the discrete two-object diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (lemma-limits-colimits), part (4), and the paragraph before it on direct sums as coproducts; Lemma 01BF (lemma-direct-sum-quasi-coherent), proof omitted

proof.text: *Choose affine descriptions.* Fix an affine open $U\subseteq X$ and identify it with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, using the affine chart [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The open immersion $j:Y\to X$ restricts each $\mathcal F_i$ to a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F_i|_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], with global sections $M_i=\mathcal F_i(U)$. By the affine tilde/global-sections equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), the counit $\varepsilon_i:\widetilde{M_i}\to\mathcal F_i|_Y$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent), proof, first sentence, using Lemma 01IB (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent); Section 01LA (section-quasi-coherent), item (1)

proof.text: *Identify the sum on $Y$.* Since $(-)|_Y$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (1), Step 1 gives that $\mathcal B|_Y$ with the restricted inclusions is a coproduct of $\mathcal F_1|_Y,\mathcal F_2|_Y$. Put $M=M_1\oplus M_2$ with its module injections $k_i$; the formula $(m_1,m_2)\mapsto u_1(m_1)+u_2(m_2)$ shows that $(M,k_1,k_2)$ is a coproduct of $M_1,M_2$ in $\mathrm{Mod}_R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (4), $(\widetilde M,\widetilde{k_1},\widetilde{k_2})$ is therefore a coproduct of $\widetilde{M_1},\widetilde{M_2}$. The isomorphisms $\varepsilon_i$ of Step 2 give the coproduct cocone $\mathcal B|_Y$ on the $\widetilde{M_i}$ with legs $j_i|_Y\circ\varepsilon_i$. The universal properties [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] supply mutually inverse morphisms $\psi:\widetilde M\to\mathcal B|_Y$ and $\chi:\mathcal B|_Y\to\widetilde M$, characterized by $\psi\widetilde{k_i}=j_i|_Y\varepsilon_i$ and $\chi j_i|_Y=\widetilde{k_i}\varepsilon_i^{-1}$; their composites are identities because they agree with identities after the two coprojections. Thus $\mathcal B|_U\cong\widetilde{M_1\oplus M_2}$ as $\mathcal O_U$-modules.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent), proof, the identification of the direct sum on an affine scheme with $\widetilde{\bigoplus M_i}$; Section 01LA (section-quasi-coherent), item (3)

proof.text: *Quasi-coherence.* Every point of the scheme $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U$ [def-pc-scheme]. Step 3 identifies $\mathcal B|_U$ with $\widetilde M$ for the $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module $M=\mathcal F_1(U)\oplus\mathcal F_2(U)$. This is the affine-neighbourhood condition defining quasi-coherence [pqf-def-coherent]. Hence $\mathcal F_1\oplus\mathcal F_2=\mathcal B$ is quasi-coherent; the empty scheme causes no exception, since the condition is vacuous.
